name: MDS/MPN overlap neoplasms (CMML)
theme: the MDS/MPN overlap · the post-HMA cliff

meta.title: CMML in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (MDS/MPN overlap neoplasm), adult
meta.population: Adults with CMML - the disease that IS a boundary: one clone wearing two faces, sitting exactly between this registry's mds and mpn trainers and pointing at both honestly. THE TWO-FACE ROUTER is the spec's spine: PROLIFERATIVE CMML (WBC >= 13, RAS-pathway biology, splenomegaly and constitutional symptoms - the MPN face) and DYSPLASTIC CMML (cytopenia-dominant - the MDS face) are routed separately because the treatment receipts themselves segregate by face: both randomized trials ever run in CMML (Wattel 1996, DACOTA) enrolled the proliferative face. An orphan-of-orphans (~1,100 US cases/year): no CMML-specific drug approval has ever existed beyond the HMA class, no phase 3 has ever been positive, and the spec carries that as VERIFIED-BY-ABSENCE rather than apology. AML transformation (blasts >= 20%) reroutes LIVE to the aml trainer.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the MDS/MPN overlap, where the registry's response-is-not-survival lesson reaches its purest form. THE TWO-FACE ROUTER: proliferative and dysplastic CMML get separate menus because the evidence segregates - and the proliferative menu carries the registry's most counterintuitive honest ranking: DACOTA (verified, the only modern phase 3 in CMML) randomized decitabine against HYDROXYUREA in advanced proliferative disease and decitabine NEARLY DOUBLED the response rate (63% vs 35%, p=.0004) while moving NOTHING that matters - EFS null (p=.27), OS null (p=.…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: WHO 5th edition + ICC 2022 (both verified): monocytosis threshold LOWERED to >= 0.5 x10^9/L with monocytes >= 10% of WBC (the oligomonocytic reclassification - receipts verified); MD-CMML (WBC < 13) vs MP-CMML (>= 13) retained; CMML-1/-2 blast bands (CMML-2: 5-19% PB / 10-19% BM or Auer rods); CPSS (Such 2013, verified - and its common MIS-CITATION caught) and CPSS-Mol (Elena 2016, verified) as the risk axis
meta.response: MDS/MPN International Working Group response criteria; the cornerstone honesty is that RESPONSE IS NOT SURVIVAL in this disease - DACOTA nearly doubled ORR and moved neither EFS nor OS

Newly diagnosed.name: Symptom-directed care, lower-risk (the neighbor disciplines)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: registry/series composite (flagged); the discipline is the neighbors' - referenced, not duplicated
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: minimal by design - the error to avoid is premature escalation
Newly diagnosed.patient: For lower-risk disease: treating symptoms and counts, not the calendar - with the published score deciding when anything more is worth its costs.
drugs: ESAs / transfusion support / hydroxyurea per face

Newly diagnosed.name: Hydroxyurea (the pill that would not be beaten - proliferative, higher-risk)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the proliferative-face backbone (randomized receipts x2 - the only ones this disease has)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized control arm, measured live (DACOTA) + the Wattel legacy win (verified)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: cytopenias, mucocutaneous - the gentlest ledger on the higher-risk menu
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the overactive form: a fifty-year-old inexpensive pill that the newer infusion drug could not beat in the one fair head-to-head trial - it controls counts and symptoms, and it holds the honest top slot.

Newly diagnosed.name: HMA, proliferative face (responses without survival - said on the card)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: label includes CMML (HMA class, secondhand; oral DEC-C verified) - the survival claim does NOT, and the card says so
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized arm measured live (DACOTA) - response benefit real, survival benefit ABSENT
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: cytopenias and infection risk through early cycles - a heavier ledger than the pill it did not beat
Newly diagnosed.patient: The infusion (or newer tablet) drug: it shrinks the disease on paper twice as often as the old pill - and in the fair test, that did not translate into living longer. It still earns its place as a bridge to transplant and for particular blood-count problems.

Newly diagnosed.name: HMA, dysplastic face (the MDS-face standard at its uncontrolled grade)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the dysplastic-face convention (label includes CMML; NCCN MDS-guideline territory secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: uncontrolled series (verified numbers, grade said) - no randomized receipt exists for this face
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: cytopenias and infection risk through early cycles
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the low-counts form at higher risk: the standard marrow-modifying drug - with the honest note that its evidence here comes from case series rather than a randomized trial, and its best role is often as the bridge to a curative transplant.

Newly diagnosed.name: Allogeneic HCT (the only cure - registry grade)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the higher-risk fit standard (registry grade; guideline convention secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: registry series (CIBMTR verified) - the only cure, never randomized
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the full transplant ledger at a median-age-71 disease - which is exactly why fitness gates it
Newly diagnosed.patient: The one path to cure: a donor transplant - a serious undertaking whose results are best when the referral starts early, before the standard drugs stop working.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining disease-directed treatment is a real choice - with transfusions and symptom care continuing as wanted.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Post-HMA therapy (the cliff, with its honest door-list)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: no approved therapy - trial doors ARE the standard, said plainly
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: natural-history receipt verified; the doors early-phase, each at its grade
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: regimen-dependent; the cliff's height argues for trial enrollment over improvisation
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: When the standard drug stops working, the honest truth is that nothing is approved next - the strongest moves are a well-chosen study or the transplant conversation, quickly, because this window is short.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Allogeneic HCT at/after failure (the cure's last window)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: the fit patient's salvage standard (registry grade)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: registry series (verified) - worse at failure than before it, said
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the full transplant ledger under time pressure
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The transplant remains the one cure even now - at tougher odds than it would have had earlier, which is exactly why the earlier conversation matters.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Comfort-focused care is a real choice - with transfusions and symptom relief continuing exactly as wanted.

CPSS-Mol at diagnosis (RUNX1/NRAS/SETBP1/ASXL1): median OS >144-to-18 months across four groups - the transplant conversation starts where the score says
transplant-eligibility review EARLY: CPSS-at-transplant predicts through the transplant (CIBMTR), and only 9% of HMA-treated patients ever reached allo-SCT (MDACC)
oligomonocytic CMML on the door: 38% become overt at 12 months

Oligomonocytic CMML receipts (both matched): same clinicopathologic/mutational profile as classical CMML (PMID 28548124) + long-term outcomes incl. 104 formerly-oligomonocytic (PMID 38013238) - why the 2022 threshold moved | PMID 28548124 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

Such et al. CPSS (Blood 2013;121:3005-15): FAB + WHO subtype + CMML-specific cytogenetics + RBC transfusion dependence -> 4 groups (558 training + 274 validation). PMID 23372164, pubmed-url-match - TRAP CAUGHT: commonly MIS-CITED as 23223431; the verified PMID is 23372164 | PMID 23372164 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

Elena et al. CPSS-Mol (Blood 2016;128:1408-17): 38 genes, 93% mutated; RUNX1/NRAS/SETBP1/ASXL1 independent for OS - genetic + clinical -> 4 groups. PMID 27385790, pubmed-url-match. GFM score (Itzykson JCO 2013, PMID 23690417 matched): ASXL1 + age + Hb + WBC + platelets; ASXL1-TET2 interaction (26771811) and ASXL1/SETBP1 two-center 466-pt study (24695057) matched | PMID 27385790 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

Itzykson et al. DACOTA (JCO 2023): decitabine vs HYDROXYUREA, advanced proliferative CMML (n=170) - ORR 63% vs 35% (p=.0004) and NOTHING ELSE: EFS 12.1 vs 10.3 (HR 0.83, p=.27 - primary NOT met), OS 18.4 vs 21.9 (p=.67, point estimate FAVORING HU). The registry's purest response-is-not-survival receipt. PMID 36455187, pubmed-url-match | PMID 36455187 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

Wattel et al. (Blood 1996;88:2480-7): hydroxyurea vs etoposide, advanced CMML - median survival 20 vs 9 months (p<10^-4): the ONLY randomized OS win in CMML history. PMID 8839839, pubmed-url-match - DIGIT-SWAP TRAP CAUGHT (not 8639819) | PMID 8839839 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

Azacitidine-in-CMML series (both matched): activity (PMID 21656746) + predictive factors (PMID 23415110: n=76, ORR 43%, CR 17%, median OS 29 months). Uncontrolled grade, said. HMA class summary: ORR ~30-49%, CR ~7-17%, no randomized OS proof in CMML; GFM decitabine phase 2 (21828134) + 2017 phase 2 (28607470) matched | PMID 23415110 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

ASCERTAIN (Lancet Haematol 2024, PMID 38135371 matched): oral decitabine-cedazuridine PK-equivalence phase 3, MDS+CMML - INQOVI FDA 2020-07 label INCLUDES CMML (secondhand). The 2025 CMML-subset paper (PMID 40524338 matched): n=33, ORR 76%, CR 21%, median OS 35.7 months - encouraging, uncontrolled, flagged. DEC-C + venetoclax phase 1/2 (38316133 matched) - investigational | PMID 38135371 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

Liu et al. CIBMTR allo-HCT in adult CMML (BBMT 2017, PMID 28115276 matched): 209 adults 2001-2012 - higher CPSS at HCT, lower KPS, marrow grafts -> inferior survival. Molecular CIBMTR analysis (35443559 matched): CPSS-Mol adds little over CPSS at transplant. SFGM-TC series (23320648 matched). THE ONLY CURE - registry grade, never randomized. EBMT ~513-pt series NOT retrieved - FLAG, not cited by PMID | REF FIX 2026-08-26: prior DOI resolved to an unrelated VRE paper (27890428); correct = Liu et al CIBMTR BBMT 2017 PMID 28115276, abstract read firsthand
Long-Term Survival Benefit after Allogeneic HCT for CMML (PMID 33039516, matched; details memory-grade) - the durability receipt at registry grade | PMID 33039516 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

Natural history of CMML treated with HMAs (Am J Hematol 2017, PMID 28370097 matched): 50% HMA failure; median OS after failure 7 months overall (4 primary / 8 secondary); ~46% of secondary failures = AML transformation. THE VERIFIED CLIFF. Supporting: suboptimal HMA response series (30964202 matched) | PMID 28370097 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

The two-face framing receipts (both matched): Contemporary Risk Stratification and Treatment of CMML (33792103) + How I diagnose and treat CMML (35236051, Blood 2022 memory-grade journal) - proliferative (WBC/neutrophils high, splenomegaly, constitutional; RAS-pathway ~30% memory-grade) vs dysplastic (cytopenia-dominant); molecular canon TET2 ~60% / SRSF2 ~50% / ASXL1 ~40% (percentages memory-grade; structure receipt-backed via 32573691 matched) | PMID 33792103 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

Ruxolitinib in CMML: phase 1 (26858309 matched) + integrated phase 1/2 (34253584 matched: n=50, RP2D 20 BID, total response 35%, symptom benefit 10/11) - phase 1/2 grade ONLY, NOT approved for CMML; the pacritinib doublet is the live successor question

THE TOMBSTONE SHELF, three endings distinguished (all dated): (1) TERMINATED-WITH-ARMS-ABOARD - sabatolimab/STIMULUS program ended 2023-12/2024-01 after MDS1+MDS2 missed; STIMULUS-MDS2 explicitly enrolled CMML-2 (secondhand); (2) DEAD-ON-PUBLISHED-FUTILITY - tagraxofusp CMML: 0 CR/PR in 37 at RP2D, final results 2025 (PMID 40919483 MATCHED; approved only for BPDCN); (3) DEAD-OF-SPONSOR-BANKRUPTCY - lenzilumab (phase 1 PMID 32294158 matched; PREACH-M Australia-only, NO published PMID - FLAG): Humanigen Chapter 11 (2024-01), assets sold - the drug did not fail, the company did. Also: ven+aza post-HMA (NCT04550442) TERMINATED for accrual; menin inhibitors are NOT a CMML door (no lesion, no trial) | PMID 40919483 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

VICTORY-1 (NCT05600894, ETCTN 10538): randomized phase 2 - oral DEC-C +/- venetoclax, newly diagnosed CMML (the LEAD disease) and MDS/MPN with excess blasts; OS and transplant rate among endpoints (KU/UChicago/UCI/Yale) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08-19, registry re-check due. The third HMA-add-on attempt after two phase-3-level failures

NCT06159491: pacritinib + azacitidine, CMML-DEDICATED (Mount Sinai, phase 1/2; newly dx or <=1 prior HMA cycle; no prior JAKi) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08-19, registry re-check due. JAK2/IRAK1/CSF1R + HMA aimed at CMML's GM-CSF-hypersensitive biology; platelet-sparing. Also seen registry-grade: pacritinib-vs-HU MP-CMML randomization NCT07033598 and pacritinib MDS/MDS-MPN NCT06303193 (NOT YET RECRUITING) - watch-list

NCT05549661: onvansertib (PLK1), R/R MYELOPROLIFERATIVE CMML (WBC>13) - Mayo, phase 1 BOIN, n~25; ASH 2025 abstract live - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08-19, registry re-check due. One of two proliferative-CMML-dedicated trials in existence

NCT04734990: seclidemstat (LSD1) + azacitidine, MDS/CMML post-HMA (MD Anderson IIT) - RESUMED 2025-02 after FDA partial hold 2024-07 lifted (history FLAGGED on the door); interim ORR 43% (n=14, uncontrolled) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08-19, registry re-check due. Basket lane beside it: tuspetinib (NCT03850574 - CMML named, amended-NCT cohort status re-check) + bexmarilimab (NCT05428969 - CMML-2 ONLY, fine print said)

ABNL-MARRO 001 (NCT04061421, MDS/MPN IWG platform: targeted agent + ASTX727; first arm itacitinib) - STATUS UNKNOWN as of 2026-08-19: nothing verifiable past ASH 2023 (phase 1b n=7); registry record inaccessible this sweep - possibly closed; RE-CHECK REQUIRED before any referral (design paper PMID 36153475 exists)
